Process: 1) Select: Choose the right standard and scope. 2) Prepare: Gap analysis and documentation. 3) Audit: Certification audit by an accredited body. 4) Maintain: Surveillance audits and recertification.
Documents: Business profile and scope; Existing process documents (if any); Organisation chart.
Key facts:
- Who certifies: Independent certification bodies (not ISO itself)
- Accreditation in India: NABCB (Quality Council of India)
- Typical validity: 3 years with annual surveillance audits
FAQs:
Q: Can I get ISO certified in a day?
A: Genuine accredited certification needs implementation and an audit. Be wary of offers of "instant" certificates from unaccredited bodies.

### Pvt Ltd & LLP Annual Compliance
URL: https://leegtech.in/business-tax/annual-compliance/
Missing annual filings leads to heavy daily late fees and can disqualify directors. We keep your company or LLP compliant all year round.

A private company must hold board meetings, hold its Annual General Meeting within six months from the end of the financial year (with the first AGM within nine months), have its accounts audited, and file financial statements (Form AOC-4) and the annual return (Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A for small companies and OPCs) with the Registrar of Companies. Directors must also complete their KYC as prescribed. Late filing attracts an additional fee for each day of delay.

An LLP must file its Annual Return in Form 11 within 60 days of the end of the financial year (by 30 May) and its Statement of Account & Solvency in Form 8 by 30 October, along with its income tax return. We set up a compliance calendar and handle every filing.

Who needs it: Private limited companies and OPCs; LLPs; Companies with pending or missed filings.
What's included: Compliance calendar; Board meeting and AGM documentation; Auditor appointment filing; AOC-4 and MGT-7/7A filing; LLP Form 11 and Form 8 filing; Director KYC and event-based filings.
Process: 1) Health check: Review past filings and pending items. 2) Calendar: Set up deadlines for the year. 3) Documents: Prepare minutes, reports and forms. 4) Filing: File on MCA and share acknowledgements.
Documents: Audited financial statements; Shareholding and director details; Previous filings and minutes; DSC of directors/partners.
Key facts:
- Company AGM: Within 6 months from financial year end (first AGM within 9 months)
- Company filings: AOC-4 (financial statements) and MGT-7/MGT-7A (annual return)
- LLP Form 11: By 30 May each year
- LLP Form 8: By 30 October each year
- Late filing: Additional fee for each day of delay
FAQs:
Q: Does a company with no business still need to file?
A: Yes. Annual filings are required even if there was no activity, unless the company is closed or obtains dormant status.
Q: Can you fix past missed filings?
A: Yes. We can file pending forms and advise on any condonation or compounding needed.

## Legal Agreements & Drafting Services
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/
From NDAs and contracts to licensing, franchise, merger, acquisition and employment agreements, our legal documents are professionally drafted and tailored to your business and IP needs. Clear contracts prevent disputes and protect the value you create.

### Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/non-disclosure-agreement/
An NDA sets clear rules on what is confidential, how it may be used and what happens if it leaks. It matters most before you share an invention, code or business plan.

In India, NDAs are contracts governed by the Indian Contract Act, 1872. A good NDA defines confidential information precisely, limits its use to a stated purpose, sets exclusions (such as information already public), fixes the duration of obligations and provides remedies including injunctions.

For inventors, an NDA is especially important because disclosure without confidentiality can affect patent novelty. NDAs must be stamped according to the stamp law of the relevant state, and electronic execution is generally valid under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Who needs it: Inventors and startups pitching to partners; Companies sharing information with vendors; Employers and consultants; Parties in M&A and investment talks.
What's included: One-way or mutual NDA drafted for your situation; Purpose, scope and exclusions defined; Term, return/destruction and remedies clauses; Stamping and execution guidance; One round of revisions.
Process: 1) Brief: Tell us who is sharing what, and why. 2) Draft: Tailored NDA drafted. 3) Review: Revisions after your feedback. 4) Execute: Stamping and signing guidance.
Documents: Party names and addresses; Nature of information and purpose of sharing; Desired confidentiality period.
Key facts:
- Governing law: Indian Contract Act, 1872
- Stamp duty: As per the stamp law of the relevant state
- E-signatures: Generally valid under the IT Act, 2000
FAQs:
Q: Is an NDA enough to protect my invention?
A: It helps, but it is not a substitute for a patent. File at least a provisional application before wider disclosure where possible.
Q: Are online templates enough?
A: Templates often miss key points such as clear definitions, remedies and jurisdiction. A tailored NDA is far easier to enforce.

### Employment Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/employment-agreement/
A well-drafted employment agreement sets expectations clearly and makes sure the IP your team creates belongs to your company.

Employment agreements in India must work within the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and applicable labour laws. Key clauses cover role, compensation, probation, notice, confidentiality, IP assignment, data protection, non-solicitation and termination.

One important point: under Section 27 of the Contract Act, agreements in restraint of trade are generally void. Post-employment non-compete clauses are therefore usually unenforceable, while restrictions during employment and well-drafted confidentiality and non-solicitation clauses are more likely to be upheld. Clear IP assignment wording is essential for startups, especially for code, designs and inventions created by employees.

Who needs it: Startups hiring their first employees; Companies updating outdated templates; Businesses hiring R&D and tech staff.
What's included: Employment agreement or appointment letter; IP assignment and confidentiality clauses; Notice, termination and garden-leave provisions; Consultant and intern variants on request.
Process: 1) Brief: Share the role, terms and policies. 2) Draft: Agreement drafted for your context. 3) Review: Revisions and finalisation.
Documents: Role details and compensation structure; Existing HR policies (if any).
Key facts:
- Restraint of trade: Generally void under Section 27, Indian Contract Act, 1872
- IP ownership: Should be expressly assigned to the employer in writing
FAQs:
Q: Can I stop an employee from joining a competitor?
A: Post-employment non-competes are generally unenforceable in India. Focus on confidentiality, non-solicitation and IP clauses instead.

### IP Licensing Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/licensing-agreement/
A licence lets others use your IP while you keep ownership and earn royalties. The terms decide how much value you capture and how well you stay protected.

Licensing agreements set scope (what is licensed), exclusivity, territory, field of use, duration, royalty structure, quality control, improvements, audit rights and termination. Each type of IP has its own rules.

Under the Patents Act, 1970, patent licences must be in writing and should be registered with the Patent Office (Section 69). Copyright licences must be in writing under the Copyright Act, 1957. For trademarks, quality control by the owner is essential to protect the brand, and permitted use can be recorded with the Registry. We draft licences that are commercially sensible and legally sound.

Who needs it: Patent owners and universities licensing technology; Brand owners licensing trademarks; Software and content owners; Companies taking a licence and needing protective terms.
What's included: Deal structure and term sheet support; Licence agreement drafting; Royalty and audit mechanisms; Registration of the licence where required.
Process: 1) Structure: Agree key commercial terms. 2) Draft: Agreement prepared and negotiated. 3) Record: Registration with the IP office where required.
Documents: IP registration details; Commercial terms agreed so far; Party details.
Key facts:
- Patent licences: In writing and registrable with the Patent Office (Section 69, Patents Act)
- Copyright licences: Must be in writing (Copyright Act, 1957)
- Trademark licences: Quality control is important to maintain distinctiveness
FAQs:
Q: Exclusive or non-exclusive licence?
A: Exclusive licences usually earn higher royalties but limit you to one licensee in the defined field and territory. The right choice depends on your market strategy.

### Franchise Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/franchise-agreement/
A franchise agreement protects your brand and systems while giving franchisees a clear, workable business relationship.

India has no single franchise statute. Franchise relationships are governed mainly by the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Trade Marks Act, 1999 (for the brand licence), the Copyright Act, 1957 (for manuals and materials), competition law and, for foreign franchisors, foreign exchange regulations.

The agreement should cover territory and exclusivity, fees and royalties, brand use and quality standards, training and support, supply arrangements, data and confidentiality, audits, renewal, termination and post-termination obligations. A registered trademark is the foundation of any franchise model.

Who needs it: Brands planning to franchise; Franchisees reviewing an agreement before signing; Master franchise arrangements.
What's included: Franchise structure advice; Franchise agreement drafting or review; Brand licence and confidentiality schedules; Supporting documents (LOI, disclosure note).
Process: 1) Model: Understand your franchise model. 2) Draft: Agreement and schedules drafted. 3) Finalise: Negotiation support and execution.
Documents: Trademark details; Fee and royalty structure; Operations manual outline.
Key facts:
- Specific franchise law: None; governed by general contract and IP law
- Brand protection: Registered trademark strongly recommended before franchising
FAQs:
Q: Should I register my trademark before franchising?
A: Yes. Franchising an unregistered brand is risky for both franchisor and franchisees.

### Vendor Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/vendor-agreement/
A vendor agreement turns a purchase order relationship into clear obligations on quality, delivery, payment, liability and IP.

Disputes with vendors usually come from unclear scope, missed timelines, quality issues or payment disagreements. A written agreement sets measurable obligations, acceptance criteria, warranties, liability limits, indemnities, confidentiality and dispute resolution.

Where vendors create deliverables such as software, designs or content, the agreement must state who owns the IP. Without a written assignment, the vendor may own it by default.

Who needs it: Businesses engaging suppliers or service providers; Startups outsourcing development or design; Vendors wanting fair terms.
What's included: Master service or supply agreement; Statement of work templates; IP and confidentiality clauses; Liability, indemnity and dispute resolution.
Process: 1) Brief: Share the commercial terms. 2) Draft: Agreement drafted. 3) Finalise: Revisions and execution.
Documents: Party details; Scope, pricing and timelines.
Key facts:
- Governing law: Indian Contract Act, 1872
- IP in deliverables: Should be expressly assigned in writing
FAQs:
Q: Do I need an agreement for every order?
A: No. A master agreement with short work orders or purchase orders for each job is usually more efficient.

### Contract Drafting & Review
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/contract-drafting/
Good contracts prevent disputes. We draft and review agreements in plain, precise language that protects your interests.

A valid contract under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 needs free consent, lawful consideration and a lawful object between competent parties. Enforceability also depends on stamping: under stamp law, an inadequately stamped instrument cannot be admitted in evidence until the duty and penalty are paid.

We draft new agreements and review agreements received from others, highlighting risks, missing protections and negotiation points. Typical documents include service agreements, consultancy agreements, partnership deeds, shareholder and founder agreements, and terms of service.

Who needs it: Startups and SMEs; Freelancers and consultants; Businesses reviewing counterparty drafts.
What's included: Drafting or review with risk notes; Negotiation points summary; Stamping and execution guidance.
Process: 1) Brief: Share your requirement or the draft. 2) Draft or review: Agreement drafted or marked up. 3) Finalise: Revisions and execution guidance.
Documents: Party details; Commercial terms or existing draft.
Key facts:
- Governing law: Indian Contract Act, 1872
- Stamping: Inadequately stamped instruments are inadmissible in evidence until duty and penalty are paid
FAQs:
Q: Can contracts be signed electronically?
A: Most commercial contracts can be signed electronically under the IT Act, 2000. Some documents, such as wills and certain property documents, are excluded.

### Merger Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/merger-agreement/
Mergers involve corporate, tax, IP and regulatory steps. We prepare the documentation and make sure IP and contracts move cleanly to the merged entity.

Mergers and amalgamations of companies in India generally take place through a scheme of arrangement approved by the National Company Law Tribunal under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013. Section 233 provides a fast-track route for eligible cases, such as mergers between small companies or between a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary.

Combinations above the thresholds in the Competition Act, 2002 need approval from the Competition Commission of India. We support the legal documentation, including the scheme, related agreements and the transfer and recording of IP such as trademarks and patents in the name of the merged entity.

Who needs it: Group companies restructuring; Businesses combining with a partner company; Startups consolidating entities.
What's included: Structure and route assessment; Scheme and agreement drafting; IP due diligence and transfer recordal; Coordination with valuers and tax advisors.
Process: 1) Assess: Choose the route: NCLT or fast-track. 2) Document: Draft the scheme and agreements. 3) Approvals: Filings and approvals. 4) Post-merger: IP and licence recordals.
Documents: Financial statements of both companies; Shareholding patterns; IP and material contracts list.
Key facts:
- Route: Sections 230–232, Companies Act, 2013 (NCLT)
- Fast-track: Section 233 for eligible companies
- Competition approval: Required above Competition Act thresholds
FAQs:
Q: Do trademarks transfer automatically on merger?
A: The rights pass under the scheme, but you should record the change of ownership with the Trade Marks Registry and the Patent Office.

### Acquisition Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/acquisition-agreement/
Whether you are buying a company, a brand or a business unit, the agreement and due diligence decide what you really get.

Acquisitions are typically structured as a share purchase (buying the shares of the company) or an asset or business transfer (buying specific assets or a business undertaking). Each has different tax, stamp duty, liability and approval implications. Cross-border deals also need to follow foreign exchange rules.

For technology and consumer businesses, IP is often the main asset. We review ownership chains, registrations, licences, employee and contractor assignments, and pending disputes, then build the right representations, warranties, indemnities and conditions into the agreement.

Who needs it: Buyers of companies, brands or businesses; Sellers preparing for a sale; Investors acquiring significant stakes.
What's included: Deal structuring support; Legal and IP due diligence; SPA / BTA / asset purchase agreement drafting; Closing documents and IP assignments.
Process: 1) Structure: Share or asset deal. 2) Diligence: Legal and IP due diligence. 3) Agreement: Drafting and negotiation. 4) Closing: Closing documents and recordals.
Documents: Target information and financials; IP portfolio list; Key contracts.
Key facts:
- Common structures: Share purchase or business/asset transfer
- Cross-border deals: Subject to foreign exchange regulations
- Competition approval: Required above Competition Act thresholds
FAQs:
Q: What is IP due diligence?
A: A review that confirms the target owns or validly licenses the IP it relies on, and that the IP is registered, enforceable and free of disputes.

### Trademark Coexistence Agreement
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/trademark-coexistence-agreement/
When two businesses use similar marks, a coexistence agreement can avoid costly opposition or litigation by setting clear boundaries.

A coexistence agreement records how each party will use its mark: the goods or services, territory, styling, channels and steps to avoid confusion. It can resolve oppositions, rectification actions and infringement disputes.

The Trade Marks Registry may consider consent or coexistence when examining applications, but it is not bound by private agreements, because public confusion is also a consideration. Careful drafting improves the chance that the agreement is respected by the Registry and works in practice.

Who needs it: Parties to a trademark opposition or dispute; Businesses with similar names in different sectors; Companies entering new markets.
What's included: Conflict assessment; Negotiation support; Coexistence agreement drafting; Filing of consent with the Registry where useful.
Process: 1) Assess: Review the marks and use. 2) Negotiate: Agree boundaries. 3) Draft: Agreement drafted and executed.
Documents: Both marks and their registrations; Details of actual use.
Key facts:
- Effect on Registry: Persuasive, but not binding on the Trade Marks Registry
FAQs:
Q: Is coexistence better than opposition?
A: Often, when both parties have genuine use and a clear way to differentiate. It saves time and cost.

### Legal Notice Drafting
URL: https://leegtech.in/legal/legal-notice/
A well-drafted legal notice often settles a dispute without going to court. Where it doesn't, it builds the record for the next step.

Some notices are mandatory before legal action. For a dishonoured cheque under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the payee must send a demand notice within 30 days of receiving information of dishonour, and the drawer then has 15 days to pay. Before suing the Government, two months' notice is generally required under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

For IP matters, a cease-and-desist notice sets out your rights and the infringing acts and demands that the infringement stop. We draft notices that are precise, legally grounded and proportionate, and we prepare careful replies when you receive a notice.

Who needs it: Businesses recovering unpaid dues; Cheque bounce cases; Brand owners facing infringement; Anyone who has received a legal notice.
What's included: Fact review and legal basis; Notice or reply drafting; Dispatch guidance (registered post, email); Advice on next steps.
Process: 1) Facts: Share documents and timeline. 2) Draft: Notice or reply drafted. 3) Send: Dispatched with proof of delivery. 4) Next steps: Follow-up strategy.
Documents: Agreements, invoices or correspondence; Cheque and return memo (for Section 138); Proof of your IP rights (for infringement).
Key facts:
- Cheque bounce notice: Within 30 days of information of dishonour; 15 days to pay (Section 138, NI Act)
- Suits against Government: 2 months' notice under Section 80, CPC
- IP infringement: Cease-and-desist notice before action is common practice
FAQs:
Q: Should I reply to a legal notice I received?
A: Usually yes. A careful reply puts your position on record. Ignoring a notice can be used against you later.

## General FAQs
Q: What services does Leegtech provide?
A: Leegtech provides IP, business registration, compliance and legal documentation services: patents, trademarks, copyright and design registration, international filings (PCT, Madrid, US, UK), company and LLP registration, Startup India, MSME, GST, FSSAI, ISO, income tax and annual compliance, and drafting of agreements and legal notices.
Q: What is the difference between a patent, trademark, copyright and design?
A: A patent protects an invention or technical innovation, a trademark protects your brand identity, copyright protects original creative works, and design registration protects the visual appearance of a product. One product can be protected by more than one of them.
Q: Does Leegtech guarantee that my patent, trademark or registration will be granted?
A: No. No one can guarantee a grant, registration or approval. Decisions are made by the relevant government authorities, such as the Indian Patent Office, the Trade Marks Registry or the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, based on the law and the facts of each case. We prepare and file your matter carefully and keep you informed at every stage, but the outcome and timelines are not in our control.
Q: Is Leegtech a government office or affiliated with IP India or MCA?
A: No. Leegtech is a private company and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any government office. You can file most applications directly on the official government portals yourself. Our professional fees are for our assistance and are separate from official government fees, which are charged at actuals.
Q: Is this website an advertisement for legal services?
A: No. This website provides general information about our services and is not a solicitation or advertisement of legal services. Using the website or submitting an enquiry does not create a lawyer–client relationship. Where the law requires a step to be handled by an advocate or a registered patent or trademark agent, it is handled only by a person who is so qualified.
Q: Are government fees included in your fees?
A: No. Official government fees are charged at actuals and are shown separately from our professional fees in your quote. Reduced official fees apply to many startups, small entities, MSMEs and individuals, and we check your eligibility.
Q: Can Leegtech help with international IP protection?
A: Yes. We assist with PCT patent applications, USA and UK patent applications, UK design registration, German utility models, Madrid Protocol trademark applications and copyright registration in Canada.
Q: When should I file a patent or design application?
A: File before you publicly disclose, launch, exhibit or sell the invention or design. A public disclosure before filing can destroy novelty, and early filing secures your priority date.
Q: Can you help me reply to a patent or trademark objection?
A: Yes. We prepare replies to patent examination reports (FER) and trademark examination reports, and support hearings, amendments and opposition proceedings. Deadlines are strict: one month for a trademark examination report and six months (extendable by three) for a patent FER.
Q: Can you register my company or startup?
A: Yes. We assist with Private Limited Company, LLP, OPC and Section 8 company registration, DPIIT Startup India recognition and MSME Udyam registration.
Q: Can I protect several aspects of the same product?
A: Yes. A patent can protect the technology, design registration the appearance, a trademark the brand, and copyright the creative content such as software code and artwork.
Q: How do I get started with Leegtech?
A: Book a free consultation online, call or WhatsApp us. We review your requirement, explain the options, process and indicative timelines, and send a written fee quote before any work begins.
